plans.note: Section 21 contains a mutual cap (greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), a consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage clarifications, and Excluded Claims covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP infringement. Check mutuality, super-cap adequacy and that payment obligations are outside the cap; 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability.

No Section 20 appears in the outline even though Section 9.3 cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' (IP infringement remedies) and 21.3 assumes indemnification obligations exist. The indemnity article appears to have been dropped; verify before marking missing.

Duplicate-numbered 12.4 imposes a 24-month, all-territory competitive-activity ban on Customer — squarely prohibited. Note the direct conflict with 12.3, which states Customer has made no non-compete or exclusivity commitment; deletion of 12.4 is the fix.

12.3 preserves supplier freedom in our favour, but 7.2 (first of two clauses numbered 7.2) forces Customer to disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider — a de facto exclusivity/right-of-first-refusal. Assess under this rule; the price-matching aspect also implicates MFN.

The first 7.2 requires Customer to disclose and match more favourable third-party offers for Vendor's benefit — an MFN running against us, contrary to 12.3. Flag under whichever of MFN/EXCLUSIVITY is the primary breach and avoid double-counting the same term.

12.4 (first instance) bars Customer from soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out, no narrowing to involved personnel, and it is one-way. Contrast 12.3, which preserves general-recruitment hiring.

Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and security/service-failure terminations (9.1–9.3, 9.5); no convenience right for Customer appears, and 2.1 expressly negates termination rights on the committed spend. Confirm no Section 9.4 exists before treating as missing.

8.2 gives 12-month auto-renewals with a 30-day Customer opt-out plus a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension; 8.3 caps uplifts at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant — verify notice window and uplift cap against playbook thresholds.

28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts — outside the accepted list — while 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts, creating a direct conflict. Target 28.1 for replacement with New York law consistent with 28.2; 28.3 escalation is acceptable.

24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and change of control; 24.4 bars Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control. Appears favourable — confirm 24.3 does not undercut 24.1.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP, but 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — contrary to owning what we pay for and inconsistent with 13.2/14.3's perpetual licence language.

13.1–13.3 give a worldwide licence extending to Affiliates and contractors, perpetual paid-up rights, transferability and limits on revocation. The revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in 14.2 conflicts; decide whether to raise that under IP rather than duplicating here.

22.1 limits Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable; 22.2 places costs on Vendor absent a 5% underpayment and bars system/data access; 22.3 protects findings. Likely compliant.

No liquidated damages, early-termination penalty or interest-penalty clause payable by Customer is apparent; 7.3 bars interest on amounts not due and 27.3 allows penalty-free termination. The take-or-pay in 2.1 is closest in economic effect but should be handled under MINCOMMIT. Note no service-credit regime is stated in the body (service-level exhibit referenced in 2.2).

19.1–19.3 give professional-services, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, whole term for hosted Services), malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties; 19.4 provides repair/re-perform with refund and termination fallback and preserves other remedies; 19.5 disclaimer is mutual and carved back. Likely compliant.

18.1 sets CGL, workers' compensation, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5,000,000 cyber coverage for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers certificates, primacy and non-limitation of liability. Check limits against playbook minimums for a health-data hosting vendor.

2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per-year, three-year take-or-pay 'without reduction or termination rights' — a walk-away term with no exit, and inconsistent with 12.3's statement that no minimum-volume commitment was made. Pair with the absence of any termination-for-convenience right.

Section 10 addresses post-termination access, Deliverable delivery and refunds and alludes to an 'agreed transition period', but no express data-return/export in a usable format or transition-assistance services obligation appears (Section 11, cross-referenced in 16.5, is absent from the outline). Likely a gap on data return and exit assistance.
